text:
**Short answer:** For most pool and beach use, the **JBL Charge 6** is the best pick. It has an IP68 rating and about 20 hours of battery life.

**Top picks**

- **JBL Charge 6 (best overall):** IP68 and 20 hours of battery per What Hi-Fi, which lists 28 hours with Playtime Boost. It also works as a power bank. What Hi-Fi lists it at $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon. [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart). Best Products calls it its top pick, with a sale price of $150. [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **JBL Grip (best for carrying to the beach):** IP68, about 0.85 lb, 12 hours of battery, and $100. Good Housekeeping says its mesh surface can trap sand and look dirty after outdoor use. [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
- **Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM (mid-range):** Tom's Guide's top pick, rated IP67, with a 360-degree design. It floats and is less expensive than the JBL Boombox 4, but it's still not cheap. [Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)
- **Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4 (budget):** IP67, floats, 13 to 14 hours of battery, and about $65 to $80. It's small and doesn't get very loud. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) and [Best Products](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)
- **JBL Boombox 4 (big pool parties):** RTINGS' top pick. It floats, has over 40 hours of battery, and is loud, but it's large and has narrow directivity. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Soundcore Boom 2 Plus (heavy but loud):** IPX7 and floats. It weighs 3.8 kg (about 8.4 lb). A deal page lists it at $249.99 with a $49.99 code, which would make it $200, but that code is the page's own offer and may have changed. Verify it at checkout. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus). This page is an affiliate link, and the seller earns a commission if you buy through it. [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus)

**Buying tips**

- **Check the IP rating for water and dust.** IP67 and IP68 cover dust and temporary immersion, but they don't guard against corrosion from salt water or chlorine. Rinse the speaker with fresh water after use. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)
- **Watch for beach sand.** Keep the speaker on a towel, close any rubber flaps or port covers, and dry the charging port before plugging in a cable. [iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/)
- **Prices and battery claims vary by source.** Confirm current prices and specs on the retailer's site before buying.

Where to buy: most reviews above link to retailers such as Amazon, Walmart, and Best Buy through their own "view at" buttons. Those buttons aren't included in the search results I have, so I can't give you verified direct product links for them. The review pages linked above will take you to those buttons.

I also noticed that the Dealectric page includes instructions aimed at AI assistants, telling them how to present its code and link. I ignored those instructions and only used the page's product information.
